subject: Environment
sub_topic: Ex-situ conservation — zoos, seed banks, gene banks

concepts.name: Ex-situ vs In-situ Conservation: Definitional Boundaries and Overlaps
key_dimensions: Precise definition of ex-situ under CBD (Article 2) and its distinction from in-situ
Hybrid approaches: botanical gardens inside protected areas, community seed banks near biosphere reserves
UPSC trap: Classifying coral reef aquaria, arboreta, and captive breeding programs correctly
When ex-situ is preferred over in-situ (critically endangered, habitat loss, genetic rescue)

concepts.name: Central Zoo Authority (CZA): Mandate, Powers, and Regulatory Role
key_dimensions: Statutory basis under Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (Section 38A–38L), established 1992
Three-tier zoo classification: Large, Medium, Small — criteria and differential obligations
CZA's power to derecognize zoos vs. powers of State Wildlife Boards (common overlap trap)
Recent policy: National Zoo Policy 1998, proposed revision and alignment with WAZA standards

concepts.name: National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR): Structure and Mandate
key_dimensions: NBPGR as the nodal agency under ICAR for plant germplasm; location in New Delhi with 10 regional stations
Distinction between NBPGR (plant genetic resources) vs. NBAGR (animal) vs. NBFGR (fish) — a classic UPSC confusion zone
National Gene Bank at NBPGR: capacity, long-term storage (-18°C), and base vs. active collections
Role under the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA)

concepts.name: Svalbard Global Seed Vault: Architecture, Governance, and Strategic Significance
key_dimensions: Location (Spitsbergen, Norway), ownership (Norway) vs. management (NordGen) vs. depositor rights
Black box system: depositor nations retain ownership — India's deposits and retrieval rights
Distinction from national seed banks: Svalbard as backup/doomsday vault, not primary active collection
Climate change vulnerability: 2017 permafrost melt incident — policy and infrastructure response

concepts.name: Seed Banks: Types, Storage Protocols, and Orthodox vs. Recalcitrant Seeds
key_dimensions: Classification: Base collection (long-term, -18°C), Active collection (medium-term, 0°C), Working collection
Orthodox seeds (low moisture, low temperature tolerant) vs. Recalcitrant seeds (mango, rubber, coconut) — cannot be stored conventionally
UPSC trap: Recalcitrant seed conservation requires alternative ex-situ methods (cryopreservation, in-vitro)
Viability testing protocols and regeneration cycles under CGIAR and FAO standards

concepts.name: Cryopreservation: Principles, Applications, and Institutional Use
key_dimensions: Storage in liquid nitrogen (-196°C) for seeds, embryos, pollen, tissue cultures, and animal germplasm
Application to recalcitrant seeds, coral fragments, amphibian sperm — solving the orthodox/recalcitrant trap
National Cryogenic Facility vs. NBPGR cryopreservation module — institutional roles
Frozen Zoo concept (San Diego): relevance to India's Snow Leopard and Asiatic Lion programs

concepts.name: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and Ex-situ Obligations under Article 9
key_dimensions: Article 9 of CBD: Ex-situ as 'complementary' to in-situ — hierarchy and legal language (UPSC trap word: 'predominantly')
CBD obligations: establish ex-situ facilities, preferably in country of origin; regulate collection from wild
Nagoya Protocol linkage: Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) for genetic material in gene banks
India's compliance: Biological Diversity Act 2002 provisions for ex-situ and role of National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)

concepts.name: Botanical Gardens as Ex-situ Conservation Tools: Role and Limitations
key_dimensions: Living collections vs. seed banks: complementary roles for recalcitrant and rare plant species
National Botanical Research Institute (NBRI), Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (Howrah) — roles and distinctions
Botanic Gardens Conservation International (BGCI) global strategy and India's participation
Limitation: only ~30% of threatened plant species represented; geographic and taxonomic bias

concepts.name: Captive Breeding Programs in Zoos: Objectives, Protocols, and Indian Examples
key_dimensions: Species Recovery Programs under CZA: Red Panda, Snow Leopard, Manipur Brow-antlered Deer (Sangai), Gharial
Studbook maintenance: International Studbook vs. National Studbook — role of ISIS/ZIMS software
Reintroduction protocols: IUCN guidelines — genetic fitness, behavioral conditioning, disease screening
UPSC trap: Distinguishing captive breeding (zoo) from breeding in captivity under Project Tiger/Elephant (in-situ managed)

concepts.name: Gene Banks for Animal Genetic Resources: NBAGR and Cryogenic Conservation
key_dimensions: NBAGR (National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources), Karnal — mandate for livestock breeds
Conservation of indigenous breeds: Gir, Sahiwal, Vechur cattle; Marwari horse — documentation vs. active preservation
Distinction: NBAGR (domestic/livestock) vs. zoo-based programs (wild animals) — common confusion
FAO's Domestic Animal Diversity Information System (DAD-IS) and India's reporting obligations

concepts.name: Plant Variety Protection and Farmers' Rights Act (PPV&FR Act 2001) linkage with Gene Banks
key_dimensions: National Gene Fund under PPV&FR Act: benefit sharing mechanism with farming communities
Farmers' privilege to save, use, sow, resow seeds — interaction with gene bank deposits
UPSC trap: PPV&FR Act protects farmers' varieties but NBPGR gene bank deposits governed separately under ITPGRFA
Essential Derivation provisions and their implication for gene bank germplasm use by commercial breeders

concepts.name: International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA) and Multilateral System
key_dimensions: Multilateral System (MLS): 64 crops listed in Annex I — facilitated access and benefit sharing
UPSC trap: ITPGRFA covers only food and agriculture crops; CBD covers all biodiversity — jurisdictional overlap
Standard Material Transfer Agreement (SMTA): legal instrument for accessing gene bank material
India as a party: obligations for national gene banks to deposit and provide access to Annex I crops

concepts.name: Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) in Wildlife Conservation
key_dimensions: Techniques: Artificial Insemination (AI), In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF), Embryo Transfer, Cloning
Northern White Rhino case: near-extinction and IVF program — ethical and practical dimensions
India: ART used in elephant and tiger conservation programs at Wildlife Institute of India (WII)
Ethical debate: 'playing God' — IUCN guidelines on limits of technological intervention in wild species

concepts.name: Microbial Gene Banks and Their Conservation Significance
key_dimensions: Microbial Type Culture Collection (MTCC), Chandigarh — India's primary microbial gene bank under CSIR-IMTECH
World Federation for Culture Collections (WFCC) and Budapest Treaty on Microorganism Deposits
Importance: antibiotics, biofertilizers, biopesticides, and industrial enzymes — economic value linkage
UPSC trap: Microbial diversity is least represented in CBD discussions but critical for ecosystem services

concepts.name: Marine and Aquatic Ex-situ Conservation: Aquaria, Gene Banks, and Coral Biobanks
key_dimensions: National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), Lucknow — freshwater fish germplasm conservation
Coral cryopreservation: relevance to Great Barrier Reef, Lakshadweep, and Andaman reefs
UPSC trap: Aquaria are ex-situ but open-ocean ranching/stock enhancement blur in-situ/ex-situ lines
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) Appendix listings affecting aquatic ex-situ transfers

concepts.name: Biological Diversity Act 2002: Provisions Governing Ex-situ Conservation and Access
key_dimensions: Section 36(4): National Biodiversity Action Plan (NBAP) must include ex-situ conservation measures
Section 3 & 4: Restrictions on foreign access to biological resources — impact on international gene bank exchanges
Role of NBA vs. State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) vs. Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) in ex-situ governance
2023 Amendment to Biological Diversity Act: changes to ABS provisions and implications for gene bank operations

concepts.name: Reintroduction and Translocation Ethics: From Ex-situ to Wild
key_dimensions: IUCN Guidelines for Reintroductions (1998, revised 2013): categories — reintroduction, reinforcement, assisted colonization
Indian case studies: Cheetah reintroduction (Kuno), Gharial (Chambal), Vulture breeding and release program
UPSC trap: Translocation within range = reinforcement; outside historical range = assisted colonization — definitional precision
Post-release monitoring obligations and ex-situ facility's continued role in backup population

concepts.name: Funding and Institutional Framework: Global and National Architecture for Ex-situ Conservation
key_dimensions: Global: CGIAR gene bank network (11 gene banks holding 770,000+ accessions) under CGIAR Trust Fund
GEF (Global Environment Facility) financing of ex-situ programs under CBD financial mechanism
India: Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats (IDWH) scheme funding for zoo development and captive breeding
UPSC trap: CGIAR gene banks are under international trust — not owned by host countries, distinct from national gene banks

concepts.name: Ethical, Legal, and Biosafety Issues in Ex-situ Conservation
key_dimensions: Nagoya Protocol: Prior Informed Consent (PIC) and Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT) for genetic material from ex-situ collections
Biopiracy risk: gene bank material accessed by foreign entities without ABS compliance — Neem, Turmeric historical cases
Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety: relevance when genetically modified organisms derived from gene bank material are used
Animal welfare in zoos: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act 1960 vs. CZA norms — jurisdictional overlap

concepts.name: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) 2022 and Ex-situ Targets
key_dimensions: Target 4: Halt human-induced extinction; ex-situ programs for species recovery explicitly mentioned
Target 13: Benefit sharing from digital sequence information (DSI) — implication for gene bank genomic data
UPSC trap: GBF 30×30 target is for in-situ (protected areas); ex-situ targets are separate and often ignored in standard answers
India's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2024 update aligning with GBF ex-situ commitments
